exposure: Infant exposure to SARS-CoV-2 infected caregivers
outcome: Infant SARS-CoV-2 antibody concentrations (S1 + S2 IgG)
cohort: The study included 46 SARS-CoV-2 infected mothers and their infants (aged 1-36 months), 26 breastfeeding mothers with no known SARS-CoV-2 infection or exposures, and 11 mothers who tested SARS-CoV-2 negative after experiencing symptoms or close contact exposure, all with their infants.
finding: Infants of SARS-CoV-2 infected mothers showed a lower probability of antibody seropositivity compared to their mothers, and the likelihood of infant infection was positively associated with maternal symptoms and other household infections, supporting minimal risks to infants, including breastfeeding infants, after maternal COVID-19 infection.
followup_time: Up to two months following maternal infection onset
